messages:
Anya Patel: FYI rolling canary for 2026.03.17 merged change 'fused-attn-scheduler' is showing a p95 tail spike on short-seq traffic :eyes:
Anya Patel: CI perf suite flagged decode.p95 +18% on canary vs baseline: https://ci.internal/reports/2026-03-17/1234 (CI alert attached)
ci-bot: [alert] perf/regression decode.p95 +18% (canary: 210ms -> baseline: 178ms) for job 'serving-decode-perf'
Mike Chen: ugh. which path? fused-attn or scheduler heuristics?
Anya Patel: profiler flame sample from canary: top: fused_attn_kernel_runner::dispatch -> attention_prefetch -> kv-cache-sync -> kernel_select. Kernel selection time increased ~40us per token on short seqs.
Anya Patel: quick paste of perf top lines:
```
fused_attn_kernel_runner::dispatch  43.2%
attention_prefetch                  11.5%
kv_cache_sync                       9.8%
kernel_selector::score_paths       7.9%
others                              27.6%
```
Kai Rodriguez: I ran a narrow bisect locally, looks like commit 8f3b1d4 (change: prefer_fused_when_benefit_est>=0.02) flips scoring so short sequences now pick fused path more aggressively.
Mike Chen: That commit touched kernel heuristics + batching thresholds. Could be bad interaction with our short-seq schedule.
Sarah L.: Are we seeing increased GPU occupancy or just host-side scheduler churn?
Anya Patel: Host-side scheduling jitter + extra kernel_select calls. For short sequences fused path has smaller kernel startup overhead but our scoring now biases it even when overhead wins. Net: more selector churn -> higher p95.
Kai Rodriguez: Reproduced with local microbenchmark. Command I used:
```
python infra/benchmarks/run_shortseq.py --model gpt-small --iters 2000 --concurrency 8
```
Result: baseline (pre-8f3b1d4) p95=160ms, post-commit p95=188ms.
Mike Chen: Can we add a quick heuristic: require benefit_est > 0.05 for seq_len<32? If that's low-risk we can hotfix and rerun canary.
Anya Patel: I pushed a draft PR with that guard: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/5247 - includes unit + microbench.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment paused (policy: p95 > baseline + 10%).
infra-monitor: Observed increased KV cache evictions coincident with rollout (small spike in kv_eviction_rate).
Kai Rodriguez: Interesting — kernel flip increases memory touch pattern causing more KV churn. That could explain extra prefetch and kv-cache-sync time.
Mike Chen: Two options: 1) revert 8f3b1d4 (fast) or 2) merge the guard in PR5247 (slower but targeted). Which is safer for rollout?
Anya Patel: Revert is simplest but loses other good cases for medium seqs. Guard has tests and microbench evidence. We should hold rollout until guard merges.
Sarah L.: Agree hold. If CI passes PR5247, we can promote after smoke tests. Add a short-lived feature-flag to quickly flip if anything else leaks.
Mike Chen: I'll kick CI on PR5247 and run canary smoke locally.
ci-bot: CI started for PR #5247 (unit, microbench, e2e-smoke).
Anya Patel: Adding tracing hooks to kernel_selector to log decision reasons in prod for next canary. Should help if there are other corner cases.
Kai Rodriguez: Also adding a small opt metric: selector_call_count per request to detect churn.
Mike Chen: Thanks — keep updates here. If CI is green and smoke looks good we'll resume rollout. For now mark this thread as rollout-blocker. :thumbsup:
Anya Patel: tl;dr: merged heuristic flip (8f3b1d4) caused fused kernel to be selected too often for short-seq -> host scheduler churn -> p95 spike. PR5247 adds short-seq guard and observability; holding rollout until validated.
Sarah L.: Filing follow-up issue to revisit scoring math and add threshold calibration in our perf tests.
Anya Patel: Filed: https://github.com/redwood/inference/issues/1889
Mike Chen: If PR5247 CI passes, I'll run canary tomorrow morning and post new measurements here.
deploy-bot: Canary resume gated on manual approval by eng-runtime after PR merge.
